trial_court: Family Court, Rangareddy District at L.B.Nagar, O.P.No.971 of 2011
case_name: K Ravinder vs K Neeraja, Tejaswi
facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife who got married in 2004. The husband filed a petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 on grounds of cruelty and desertion.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking dissolution of marriage to plead and prove the grounds for such relief.
legal_principles.held: As discussed supra, it is the appellant who filed the aforesaid O.P. seeking dissolution of marriage on the grounds of cruelty and desertion. Therefore, burden lies on him to plead and prove the same by adducing cogent evidence.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not intervene in a marriage unless the parties have exhausted all reasonable avenues of reconciliation.
legal_principles.held: He along with the respondent lived in one Doctor's house as tenant for four to five years. ... He has further admitted that he has not seen the instances of cruelty of the respondent towards the appellant and the same were happened only in front of the parents of the appellant.

outcome.final_order: Sending notice to the respondent to the address available in the bundle is sufficient in terms of Section 27 of the General Clauses Act.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on unserved notice in family court proceedings
